newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Wednesday:

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said the Commission would hold its weekly meeting at 1500/1300 GMT in Strasbourg and spokesmen would be available to provide notes and answer questions from 1530/1330 in their respectives offices.

Spokeswoman Sarah Lambert said the Commission had received a delegation from Italian airline Alitalia on Tuesday to discuss details of the plan to revitalise the company. Lambert said the Commission had not yet decided whether to accept the Italian view that the plan as an ordinary capital injection or that it was state aid. She said the Commission hoped to have the decision by the end of October.
Vale de Almeida said Commissioner Anita Gradin's speech to the European Parliament on paedophilia would be available in spokeswomen Sophie Petzell's office at 1700/1500 GMT.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/834: New challenges for the Euro Info Centres (EIC) network.
- IP/96/835: Luxembourg benefits from European Social Fund.
- IP/96/837: Commission clears Verlagsgruppe Handelsblatt state in N-TV.
- IP/96/838: Commission approves joint venture of Schering and Gehe in Jenapharm.
- IP/96/839: "Urgent need for action to curb radiation risks from the Chernobyl sarcophagus" - Statement by Commissioner Bjerregaard and Commissioner van den Broek.
- IP/96/840: The European Commission hosts a conference: Global comparaison of regional RTD and innovation strategies for development and cohesion.
- Speech/96/216: Address by Commission President Jacques Santer to the European Parliament on "The state of the Union".
- Eurostat: News release, No 58/96: Traditional EU12 family "is being eroded".
- Eurostat: Statistics in focus, population and social conditions, 1996 No 5: Under the same roof, Living arangements in the European Union.
